id: 313-李錫尼與馬克西米努斯·戴亞的戰爭
theater: 色雷斯與比西尼亞海岸

battle.name: 李錫尼與馬克西米努斯·戴亞的戰爭
battle.theater: 色雷斯與比西尼亞海岸
battle.brief: 公元313年，四帝制崩解的羅馬帝國裡，東方奧古斯都馬克西米努斯·戴亞與凱撒李錫尼開戰。戴亞在色雷斯的冬季遠征耗盡兵員，未能進安條克，5月病歿於塔爾蘇斯，李錫尼遂獨佔東方。卡面的斯巴達長矛出自公元前八世紀的希臘方陣，而到313年站在戰線上的是它更沉重的同族：羅馬軍團的重標槍。

kit.name: 斯巴達長矛
kit.history: 兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套。方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站住了。

countries: 這場戰爭是羅馬帝國四帝制崩解之後的內戰中段，交戰的兩方在法理上都自稱羅馬人。東方奧古斯都馬克西米努斯·戴亞是戴克里先的外甥，305年受封凱撒，311年加利里烏斯在西爾米烏姆病逝後獨佔亞洲，以尼科米底亞與安條克為治所；其下有凱撒李錫尼與次子馬克西米努斯二世。另一方是李錫尼：308年卡農圖姆會議上被列為東方奧古斯都，311年後被迫降為戴亞的凱撒，駐節色雷斯與馬其頓。戴克里先293年設立的四帝制刻意規定皇位按功績而非血緣傳遞，但305年兩位奧古斯都自稱神明、306年兩位相繼退位而軍隊立刻推舉新主，這條原則早已耗盡它的約束力，帝國實際上分給了六位共治者。軍隊體系是晚期羅馬的常備軍：以軍團為唯一作戰單位，配合輔助兵與野戰騎兵，每位皇帝另有自己的親衛軍與個人追隨者；效忠靠軍糧、薪給與賞賜維持，合法性則一半靠軍隊推立、一半靠元老院授銜。第三方陣容同樣真實存在：安條克一類城市的議會可以關閉城門拒絕皇帝入城，非洲的主教爭端牽涉東西方各自的教會支持，而元老院與造幣廠決定誰的名字能被刻上銅幣。
countriesEn: This war is a middle chapter of the civil wars that followed the collapse of the Tetrarchy, and both sides claimed in law to be Romans. The eastern Augustus, Maximinus Daia, was Diocletian's nephew; he was made Caesar in 305 and, after Galerius died at Sirmium in 311, held Asia alone, with Nicomedia and Antioch as his seats; under him were the Caesar Licinius and his own son, Maximinus II. The other side was Licinius: named eastern Augustus at the conference of Carnuntum in 308, he was pushed back down to the rank of Caesar after 311 and based himself in Thrace and Macedon. The Tetrarchy that Diocletian had set up in 293 deliberately made the imperial office pass by achievement rather than by blood, but when both Augusti claimed divinity in 305 and then abdicated in 306, and the troops promptly acclaimed new emperors, that principle had already been drained of force; the empire was in fact divided among six rulers. The military system was that of the late Roman standing army: the legion as the only tactical unit, supported by auxiliaries and field cavalry, with every emperor keeping his own guard and his own personal following. Obedience was maintained through pay, rations and donatives, while legitimacy was half created by the soldiery and half by the senate's grant of titles. There were real third parties too: the councils of cities such as Antioch could close their gates against an emperor, the dispute between bishops in Africa drew in the church backing of each half of the empire, and the senate and the mints decided whose name could be struck in bronze.
people: 關鍵人物可分三類。君主一方是馬克西米努斯·戴亞（馬庫斯·奧勒留·瓦勒里烏斯·馬克西米安努斯，號戴亞）：他以嚴酷與貪婪著稱，311年自升為奧古斯都，據說下令把自己錢幣上的「dominus et deus」稱號撤下，312年入侵義大利反被自己部隊拋棄，313年初再圖於色雷斯翻盤，5月病歿於奇里乞亞的塔爾蘇斯，一般相信是他自己收買的醫師下的手。另一方是李錫尼（瓦勒里烏斯·李錫尼安努斯·李錫尼）：被加利里烏斯任為凱撒、308年升為奧古斯都、311年降回凱撒、313年因戴亞之死重掌東方；他與戴克里先是姻親，其妻君士坦丁娜是君士坦丁同母異父的妹妹，這門婚姻與米蘭會盟把東方和西方綁在一起。第三類是推手與記錄者：君士坦丁此時已是西部唯一的奧古斯都，兩度獲得元老院授銜，又在313年2月與李錫尼共同頒下米蘭敕令；非洲的兩位主教卡奇利安與多納圖斯因教會權力爭端公開分裂，雙方背後都有帝王的影子；留下記錄的則有拉克坦西烏斯《迫害者之死》、尤西比烏斯同名的《迫害者之死》、佐西莫斯《新史》、歐特羅皮烏斯《綱要》與奧勒留斯·維克托《諸凱撒》，他們各自站在不同位置，卻共同把313年這場幾乎沒有會戰的戰爭保存了下來。
peopleEn: The key figures fall into three groups. On the imperial side was Maximinus Daia (Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximianus, called Daia), known for harshness and greed: he raised himself to Augustus after Galerius' death in 311, is said to have had the title 'dominus et deus' struck off his own coinage, was thrown away by his own troops when he invaded Italy in 312, and died of illness at Tarsus in Cilicia in May 313, by general belief poisoned by a physician he had himself bought. The other side was Licinius (Valerius Licinianus Licinius), made Caesar by Galerius, raised to Augustus in 308, reduced to Caesar again in 311 and restored to sole rule of the East by Maximinus' death; he was a kinsman of Diocletian, and his wife Constantina was Constantine's half-sister, and that marriage and the meeting at Milan tied the East to the West. A third group are the movers and the record-keepers: Constantine, by now the only Augustus in the West, twice honoured by the senate and co-signatory of the edict of Milan in February 313; Caecilian and Donatus in Africa, whose dispute over church authority became a schism with emperors standing behind it; and the writers who preserved a war that had almost no battlefield — Lactantius in On the Deaths of the Persecutors, Eusebius in a work of the same name, Zosimus in the New History, Eutropius in the Breviarium and Aurelius Victor in On the Caesars, each standing in a different place and each giving a different angle on the same year.
kits: 卡面是斯巴達長矛（多利矛）：約兩公尺長的白木柄，葉形鐵矛頭，尾端套一圈青銅（saurotra），是公元前八世紀希臘方陣的標準兵器。它的現役生涯早在公元313年之前一千一百多年就結束了，留在這張卡上是作為對照件：多利矛的邏輯是先決定站位再決定勝負，而真正站在313年戰線上的是它的遠房表親——羅馬軍團的重標槍（pilum）。重標槍同樣約兩公尺、葉形矛頭、尾端留一枚小鐵錐，投出去可以釘住對手的大盾、把盾面扯歪；圖拉真時代又加入鉛芯的半投槍（semi-artillaria plumbata），圓錐頭、份量更重，用來在遠程壓制落单的騎兵。近戰是短劍配橢圓弧面大盾，三列縱隊 hastati、principes、triarii 早在三世紀中葉就隨戰制改革被取消，軍團改採縮編小分隊的新制度。裝備上的其他成員還包括角盔兵（cornuti）與盾兵（scutarii）等重裝輔助兵、騎兵較長的直刀（spatha）與投槍、蠻族傭兵使用的圓盾與短劍，以及整套旗制——軍團的鷹旗（aquila）仍是最重要的象徵物。攻城方面，本戰爭前幾年羅馬人仍在使用最老式的攻城技術：撞槌、攻城塔、拋石機，以及可攜式的野戰營地；而安條克與塔爾蘇斯之間逾一千公里的陸路與地中海航線，決定了後方補給的長度，也決定了遠征的成敗。
kitsEn: The card shows a Spartan dory: a two-metre ash shaft, a leaf-shaped iron head and a bronze-shod butt spike, the standard weapon of the Greek phalanx of the eighth century BC. Its working life had ended more than eleven centuries before AD 313, and it appears here as a reference piece: the logic of the dory is that the standing ground is settled before the killing is, while what actually stood on the line in 313 was its distant cousin, the Roman legionary's heavy pilum. The pilum was likewise about two metres long, with a leaf-shaped head and a small iron butt spike, thrown to pin the enemy's great shield and wrench it askew; under Trajan it was joined by the plumbata semi-artillaria, a weighted javelin with a conical head for long-range pressure on cavalry. Close work was the gladius with the curved oval scutum, and the three-line order of hastati, principes and triarii had already been scrapped in the mid-third century in favour of the new system of miniatures. The rest of the equipment included auxiliaries in the heavy style such as the cornuti and scutarii, cavalry with the longer spatha and throwing javelins, federate barbarian auxiliaries with round shields and short swords, and the whole flag system, in which the legionary eagle remained the central emblem. On the siege side the Romans were still using the oldest technology of all: rams, towers, stone-throwing artillery and the portable marching camp; and the more than a thousand kilometres of road and sea lane between Antioch and Tarsus set the length of the supply chain, and with it the make or break of any distant expedition.
tactics: 313年這場衝突留下的陣戰細節很少，留下來的多是戰役過程與軍隊狀態的記錄，而這本身就是它的戰術特徵。東方軍隊在色雷斯的推進方向大致是從博斯普魯斯海峽渡過之後向西，指向赫布羅斯河；那是一次冬季作戰，拉克坦西烏斯描述軍隊在雪地與泥濘中行軍、糧秣不足、士兵大批逃亡。到了安條克這一步，城市議會關閉城門拒絕皇帝及其隊伍入城，戴亞的軍隊在城外失去補給，也失去象徵性的城市支持，這一點同他在義大利的遭遇完全一致：312年他進攻米蘭與北意大利，結果自己的軍隊拒絕為他作戰。士氣與效忠才是這場戰爭真正的兵種。軍隊本身的戰法，這時仍是Principate 的老樣子：軍團與輔助兵以密結陣縱隊前進，標槍先投、短劍後進，兩翼由騎兵與精銳分隊（vexillatio）施壓，親衛軍在陣前；野戰營地按標準尺寸挖掘壕溝與木柵，皇帝旗與軍團旗分列左右。可是在313年，這套東西的價值被高估了：真正決定東西方勝負的，是行政與象徵手段——把對手在安條克的銅像投入河中，把對方在海上的銅像投入海中，以米蘭敕令獨佔宗教合法性的解釋權，並且在對方的城市與教會裡扶持自己的人。戴亞最後不是死於戰場，而是死於病榻，這正是這場戰爭最耐人尋味的地方。
tacticsEn: Very little about the actual fighting in 313 survives, and what does survive is mostly an account of how a campaign was run and of the condition of the troops — which is itself the tactical character of this war. The eastern column moved west through Thrace after crossing the Bosporus, aiming at the river Hebros; it was a winter campaign, and Lactantius describes the army marching through snow and mud, short of food, with large numbers of deserters. At Antioch the city council shut its gates against the emperor and his train, so the army lost both its supply and the symbolic backing of the city — exactly as in Italy, where in 312 Maximinus' own troops refused to fight for him. Morale and allegiance, not manoeuvre, were the decisive weapon in this war. The army's own methods were still those of the Principate: legionaries and auxiliaries advanced in close order, javelins first and the sword after, with cavalry and elite vexillations pressing the flanks and the imperial guard in front; the marching camp was dug to a standard plan with ditch and palisade, and the imperial and legionary standards stood on either side. But in 313 that apparatus was overrated. What really decided the struggle between east and west were administrative and symbolic measures: throwing the rival's bronze statue into the river at Antioch and his counterpart into the sea, claiming the exclusive right to interpret religious legitimacy through the edict of Milan, and supporting each other's rivals inside the rival's own cities and churches. Maximinus did not die on a battlefield but on a sickbed, which is the strangest fact about this war.
data: 先列能核對的日期與數字。313年2月13日，君士坦丁與李錫尼在米蘭頒下宗教容忍敕令，結束戴克里先自303年開始的大迫害；同年4月5日，李錫尼在米蘭迎娶君士坦丁娜；8月21日，君士坦斯二世生於西爾米烏姆，這是這場戰爭的意外產物。往前推：戴克里先一系在305至308年間以「dominus et deus」自我神化；306年7月25日君士坦丁在不列顛被軍隊推舉；308年卡農圖姆會議上五名凱撒同時被指定，李錫尼在此被列為東方奧古斯都；310年馬克西米安在馬西利亞被處決，戴亞隨後把自己錢幣上的神化稱號撤下；311年11月加利里烏斯在西爾米烏姆病逝，戴亞獨佔東方；313年5月戴亞死於塔爾蘇斯。地理方面，從博斯普魯斯海峽到赫布羅斯河約三百公里，安條克到塔爾蘇斯沿陸路逾一千公里，海運航線還要繞行西里西亞南部。兵力數字方面，這場戰爭沒有留下可靠的本役統計：拉克坦西烏斯與佐西莫斯描述的是軍隊的狀態而不是數目，唯一的量級參照來自歐特羅皮烏斯對幾年後李錫尼對君士坦丁之戰的記述，東方軍隊在十萬量級——那是316至317年的另一場戰爭的數字，只能用來說明313年東方可支配的軍力規模，不能當作本役的實數。傷亡方面同樣沒有可用的記載：這場戰爭幾乎沒有真正的會戰，傷亡的規模被嚴冬、饑餓與疾病壓過了戰鬥。
dataEn: Begin with the dates and figures that can be checked. On 13 February 313 Constantine and Licinius issued the edict of religious toleration at Milan, ending the great persecution begun by Diocletian in 303; on 5 April of the same year Licinius married Constantina at Milan; on 21 August Constantius II was born at Sirmium, an unexpected product of this war. Working backwards: the house of Diocletian had claimed divinity for the emperor under the title 'dominus et deus' between 305 and 308; on 25 July 306 Constantine was acclaimed by the troops in Britain; at the conference of Carnuntum in 308 five Caesars were named at once, and Licinius was among them as eastern Augustus; in 310 Maximian was executed at Massilia, and Daia then had the divine title struck off his coinage; in November 311 Galerius died at Sirmium and Daia took the East alone; in May 313 Daia died at Tarsus. In geography it is about three hundred kilometres from the Bosporus to the Hebros, and more than a thousand kilometres by road from Antioch to Tarsus, with the sea route running a long haul round southern Cilicia. On numbers of men there is no dependable return for this war: Lactantius and Zosimus describe the state of the army rather than its size, and the only order-of-magnitude marker comes from Eutropius' account of Licinius' war against Constantine a few years later, where the eastern field army stands in the region of a hundred thousand foot — figures belonging to the campaigns of 316 and 317, useful only as an indication of the military resources the East could mobilize, not as returns for this battle. There are no usable casualty figures either, for the simple reason that almost no pitched battle was fought: the losses that mattered were inflicted by the severity of the winter, by hunger and by disease.
cause: 打起來的直接原因有四層。最外層是四帝制本身：293年戴克里先把帝國分給四帝，規定皇位按功績而非血緣傳遞，但305年兩位奧古斯都自稱神明、306年兩位相繼退位而軍隊立刻推舉新主，制度的約束力其實早已耗盡。308年卡農圖姆會議是這條裂痕最集中的一次：五名凱撒同時被指定，李錫尼被加封為東方奧古斯都，戴亞的次子馬克西米努斯二世只拿到凱撒，這等於當著全軍的面削去戴亞的頭銜，他的不滿由此積累。第二層是311年加利里烏斯之死留下的權力真空：戴亞趁勢升為唯一的東方奧古斯都，李錫尼被壓回凱撒的地位，東方的軍隊效忠與城市的態度都各自往兩邊分。第三層是宗教：戴亞延續大迫害，在小亞細亞焚燒教堂、逼迫主教，安條克一帶因信仰而起的衝突屢見不鮮；與此同時非洲的主教爭端已經分裂，李錫尼在東方支持多納圖斯一派，君士坦丁在西部支持卡奇利安一派，教會的裂縫被兩位皇帝各自拿來當籌碼。第四層是米蘭：313年2月的敕令把東西兩位奧古斯都綁在同一份協議上，戴亞既被排除在外，又面對一位握有西部兵力的對手；安條克把李錫尼的銅像投入河中，李錫尼把戴亞的銅像投入海中，這一來一往撕破了最後的體面。對戴亞而言，開戰其實是被逼的：他不打，就等於在兩位奧古斯都的合圍下慢慢失去一切。
causeEn: There are four layers to the immediate cause. The outermost is the Tetrarchy itself: in 293 Diocletian divided the empire and insisted that the office pass by achievement rather than by blood, but when both Augusti claimed divinity in 305 and then abdicated in 306, and the troops promptly acclaimed new emperors, the system's binding force had already been spent. The conference of Carnuntum in 308 is where that crack shows most clearly: five Caesars were named at once, Licinius was raised to eastern Augustus, and Daia's younger son received only the rank of Caesar — a public demotion of Daia in front of the whole army, and the seed of his grievance. The second layer is the vacuum left by Galerius' death in 311: Daia rose to be the single eastern Augustus, Licinius was pressed back to Caesar, and the loyalties of the eastern army and of the cities pulled in opposite directions. The third layer is religion: Daia continued the great persecution, burning churches in Asia Minor and pressing bishops, and clashes born of faith were repeated around Antioch; at the same time the African episcopal dispute had already split, with Licinius backing the Donatian party in the East and Constantine the Caecilian party in the West, so the schism in the church became a countersignature in the hands of two emperors. The fourth layer is Milan: the edict of February 313 bound the eastern and western Augusti in a single document, leaving Daia outside it and facing an opponent who held the armies of the West; the bronze statue of Licinius thrown into the river at Antioch and the statue of Daia thrown into the sea in return stripped away the last pretence of civility. For Daia the decision to fight was in effect forced: not to fight meant losing everything by slow encirclement.
impact: 這場戰爭的直接結果是一個帝國同時存在兩位奧古斯都，而它的長期影響遠比戰役本身更深。宗教方面，313年的米蘭敕令與大迫害的終結，使基督教從一個受容忍的社團變成可以公開集會、擁有財產並行使自己司法權的合法存在；教會內部隨即浮出兩道裂痕：非洲的多納圖斯之爭捲入政治，羅馬會議與阿爾勒會議都曾介入，亞歷山大的阿里烏斯也在313年前後被立為主教，爭論最終通向325年的尼西亞公會議。帝制方面，戴亞撤下「dominus et deus」的做法證明皇帝的神性稱號可以收回也可以再戴上；此後帝國的權力結構在三十年間從四帝、六帝、兩帝一路收到一人身上，314至324年君士坦丁與李錫尼的戰爭是這條線的下一段，324年克律索波利斯一役之後帝國才真正合為一人。軍隊與制度方面，四帝制末期每位皇帝各有自己的追隨者、各自的禁衛軍、各自的錢幣與造幣廠，這種分散的軍事資源在313年被證明既是內戰的燃料，也是內戰結束後難以立刻收編的負擔；晚期的軍團制度、薪給與賞賜、土地與退役安置等問題，都要到四世紀才逐漸成形。對研究武器史的人而言，這一役還留下一個對照：公元313年早沒有人再拿多利矛上陣，但把長矛變成投射武器、把盾牆變成可以互相釘死的防線的思路，仍然是這支部隊的骨架。
impactEn: The immediate result of this war is an empire with two Augusti, but its long-run consequences reach far beyond the campaign. In religion, the edict of Milan in 313 and the end of the great persecution turned Christianity from a tolerated association into a legal body with the right to assemble, to hold property and to exercise its own jurisdiction; two cracks then opened inside the church: the Donatian affair in Africa became political, and the councils of Rome and Arles both intervened, while Arius was made bishop of Alexandria around 313 — a dispute that was to end at the council of Nicaea in 325. In the constitution of the empire, Daia's removal of 'dominus et deus' showed that the divine title of the emperor could be withdrawn as well as assumed; over the next thirty years the number of rulers contracted from four, through six and two, down to one, with the war between Constantine and Licinius in 314–324 as the next stage of that line, and the empire becoming truly single only after the battle of Chrysopolis in 324. In armies and institutions, the late Tetrarchy had given every emperor his own following, his own guard, his own coinage and his own mint; the dispersal of military resources was proved in 313 to be both the fuel of civil war and the burden that could not be absorbed once it ended, and the questions of the late legion, of pay and donatives, of land and of settlement for veterans were only worked out gradually in the fourth century. For anyone studying the history of weapons the case also leaves a reference: by AD 313 nobody was fighting with a dory any more, but the idea of turning the spear into a missile, and the shield wall into a line that can be pinned against each other, is still the skeleton of that army.
result: 結局由三件事組成：色雷斯的冬季耗盡了戴亞的軍隊，安條克的城門對他關閉，313年5月他病歿於塔爾蘇斯；李錫尼隨即成為東方唯一的奧古斯都，戴亞的凱撒兒子馬克西米努斯二世隨後被處決，東方的政權與軍隊一次性地轉入李錫尼之手。這場戰爭幾乎沒有會戰的勝負：最接近戰役的一次色雷斯遠征以冬天的失敗收場，戰爭的真正結果通過環境、疾病與城市態度慢慢顯現——這也是它在編年史裡長期被當作一場沒有戰役的戰爭的原因。戰後的帝國是兩位奧古斯都分治：不列顛、西歐與北非歸君士坦丁，亞洲與埃及歸李錫尼，兩人都以四帝制的語言為自己辯護，卻都知道對方是暫時的。312年君士坦丁在米爾維安橋擊敗馬克森提烏斯，313年戴亞死於塔爾蘇斯，這兩步把西部與東部分別騰空，帝國在疆域最大的時候由兩個人分著；而正是在這個時候，基督教不再需要迫害者，帝國也不再需要四個皇帝。對兵器史而言還有一點值得記下：這場戰爭裡沒有任何一件武器贏下局面，贏的是後勤、合法性與城市，而卡面上那把公元前八世紀的斯巴達長矛，只是替它們作了註腳。
resultEn: The outcome was made of three things: the winter in Thrace wore out Daia's army, the gates of Antioch were shut against him, and in May 313 he died at Tarsus; Licinius at once became the only Augustus in the East, Daia's Caesar-son Maximinus II was later put to death, and the government and the forces of the East passed in a single stroke into Licinius' hands. Almost no battle decided this war: the closest thing to a campaign, the expedition into Thrace, ended in a winter's defeat, and the true result of the war declared itself slowly through the weather, through disease and through the temper of the cities — which is why the chronicles long treated it as a war without a battle. What followed was a partition: Britain, the West and North Africa under Constantine, Asia and Egypt under Licinius, both of them justifying themselves in the language of the Tetrarchy while each knew the other was temporary. Constantine's victory over Maxentius at the Milvian Bridge in 312 and Daia's death at Tarsus in 313 emptied the West and the East in turn, so that the empire, at the moment of its greatest extent, was held by two men; and it was precisely then that Christianity no longer needed a persecutor and the empire no longer needed four emperors. One last note for the history of arms: no weapon won this war. Supply, legitimacy and the cities won it, and the dory on the card, a Spartan spear of the eighth century BC, is only the footnote to them.
